brief: Gladys Aylward was born in London in 1902. She spent her adult life as a missionary to the Chinese people, mainly in Yangcheng. She became a Chinese citizen, and was appointed by Chiang Kai-Shek to assist with the suppression of the custom of foot-binding. She is best remembered for her journey through the mountains in 1940 with Chinese children fleeing from the Japanese invaders. After 1957 she worked in Taiwan. She died there in 1970.
